designSequence.waveName: Generic Diagnostics, Error Handling, and Publication

purpose: Define the reusable optional Error Handling capability as a specialized Supporting Pattern, including its generic type boundaries, unit/association/lifecycle ownership, operation-result aggregation, and dependency isolation, without promoting any consumer Error Model into GPWCF Core.

included: The logical boundary and ownership of the optional Error Handling Supporting Pattern.
The generic Error Handling Unit callable and per-operation result model.
The separation of Error Handling Unit, ErrorResult, ErrorHandlerResult, and source Error Occurrences.
The Step-specialized target occurrence reference boundary.
The relationship among Error Handling Unit, Step-specific Error Handling Composition, OperationEntryPublisher, PublicationReservation, and Recovery Owner.
The generic-to-specialized dependency boundary and Public API allocation.
excluded: A universal Error Model, Error Type Definition, Error Occurrence, Error Registry, or ErrorResult schema.
A universal error taxonomy, severity model, resolution guarantee, retry policy, or failure enum.
A universal Error Handling Unit base class shared with Validation and Observation.
A central Error Handling Manager, global Publisher, plugin registry, or runtime mediator.
A universal concrete Publisher storage/concurrency implementation.
A universal Single Step Publication policy for all Steps.

governingArchitecture.classification: Optional reusable Supporting Pattern owned by the Step specialization when selected.
governingArchitecture.functionalPurpose: Execute one or more authorized handling operations against target occurrences/resources made available by the owning Step and publish the resulting operation entries through the Step-specific publication contract.
governingArchitecture.stepCompositionOwnership: Step Composition selects the Error Handling Unit, establishes/ends its Association, authorizes invocation, supplies the invocation-scoped Publisher capability, coordinates lifecycle, and integrates accepted entries into the Step-specific ErrorHandlerResult.
governingArchitecture.unitOwnership: The Error Handling Unit owns its operation execution and each THandlingOperationResult it produces until the publication acceptance/custody transfer point. It does not own source Error Occurrences, ErrorResult, StepExecutionResult, or Step flow.
governingArchitecture.errorModelOwnership: The concrete Step Error Model owns source error definitions, occurrences, references, and ErrorResult semantics. The Error Handling capability consumes authorized read-only target access and does not redefine that model.
governingArchitecture.publicationOwnership: The Step-specific Error Handling Composition owns the Publisher capability and accepted-entry storage. The Unit receives an invocation-scoped capability and does not own the Publisher.
governingArchitecture.optionalNature: A Step may select no, one, or multiple specialized Error Handling Units. The framework does not require Error Handling for every Step or SPU.

semanticDistinctions.errorOccurrence: A specialized source-domain occurrence classified by the owning Error Model. Error Handling may inspect/reference it under bounded access but does not own or mutate it.
semanticDistinctions.errorResult: The Step Error Model's aggregate/representation of source error occurrences. It remains separate from the operation results produced while handling those occurrences.
semanticDistinctions.handlingOperationResult: The specialized result of one actual handling operation. It describes what that operation produced and does not by itself prove that the target occurrence was resolved.
semanticDistinctions.errorHandlerResult: The Step-specific aggregate of accepted Error Handling operation entries. It preserves operation identity, target references, result values, and publication provenance.
semanticDistinctions.failure: A contract-specific failure to fulfill an operation or publication obligation. No universal Failure type is introduced.
semanticDistinctions.exception: A thrown invocation/operation exception. It is not automatically an Error Occurrence, HandlingOperationResult, or ErrorHandlerResult entry.
semanticDistinctions.diagnostic: Optional descriptive evidence that may accompany a specialized violation/result. It does not replace acceptance knowledge, failure semantics, custody, or domain outcome.
semanticDistinctions.prefectState: Native operational execution evidence. It is not an Error Occurrence, ErrorResult, HandlingOperationResult, or ErrorHandlerResult.

architecturalOptions.name: PromoteConsumerErrorModel
architecturalOptions.description: Move Error Type Definitions, Error Occurrences, registries, and ErrorResult into a universal Core Error Model.
disadvantages: Promotes Generator-specific registry and ownership assumptions.
Erases the distinction between SPU-level, Stage-level, and consumer-specific error families.
Makes an Error Model mandatory for consumers that may not need one.
Conflates error classification with the separate Error Handling capability.

architecturalOptions.name: UniversalSupportingUnit
architecturalOptions.description: Make Error Handling, Validation, and Observation implementations conform to one common SupportingUnit interface/result.
disadvantages: Collapses distinct invocation cardinality, output, event, association, lifecycle, and custody semantics.
Creates an unowned universal abstraction and runtime adaptation pressure.

architecturalOptions.name: SpecializedOptionalErrorHandling
architecturalOptions.description: Keep Error Handling as its own optional pattern package. Use existing generic input/result/publication contracts while keeping concrete occurrence references and Error Models Step/consumer-owned.
advantages: Preserves existing specialized contracts and ownership.
Supports different source error families without a universal Error base.
Keeps publication and recovery semantics explicit.
disadvantages: Concrete Step specializations must bind their own target occurrence and operation result types.
Each Step selecting publication must complete its concrete Publisher/Reservation proof.

selectedDesign.decision: Retain Error Handling as an optional specialized Supporting Pattern. Reuse the existing generic callable/operation/publication contracts; keep all Error Model semantics and concrete publication policy outside the generic Core Error Handling module.

module.selectionRule: A consumer imports this package only when a concrete Step selects Error Handling.

errorHandlingUnit.meaning: One Unit invocation may perform zero, one, or multiple handling operation attempts and publishes one structured operation entry for each operation execution that produces a result.
errorHandlingUnit.inputOwnership: The concrete Step defines TErrorHandlingUnitInput, including the exact Association context, operation context, authorized target-occurrence access, and required configuration/dependencies.
errorHandlingUnit.operationResultOwnership: The concrete Error Handling Unit defines THandlingOperationResult for one actual operation execution, not for the whole Unit invocation.
errorHandlingUnit.normalReturn: Normal return means the Unit invocation completed normally. It does not imply zero operations, zero results, or that all targeted errors were resolved.
errorHandlingUnit.exception: An exception remains distinct from a returned operation result. If a result was already produced before the exception, the Unit and Step-specific Recovery Owner preserve its custody.

targetOccurrenceReferenceBoundary.owner: Concrete Step Error Model and its specialized target access contract.
targetOccurrenceReferenceBoundary.meaning: A typed reference to the exact source occurrence/resource that a handling operation is authorized to inspect or target.
rules: The generic Error Handling package does not define a universal ErrorOccurrence base class or generic TErrorTargetReference type.
The concrete Step supplies the exact HandledErrorOccurrenceReference type and read-only resolution/access capability in TErrorHandlingUnitInput.
The reference preserves the source producer identity and occurrence identity required by the Step Error Model.
The Unit receives access only to targets authorized by the selected Association and input contract.
The Unit cannot create replacement source occurrences or mutate ErrorResult.

operationEntry.meaning: One complete immutable record of one actual handling operation execution, including its Unit/Association/target/invocation/attempt/operation identities and specialized result.
operationEntry.targetReferenceRule: Target occurrence references are defined by the concrete Step Error Model and carried in the specialized entry representation; they are not generalized into a Core ErrorOccurrence base type.
minimumSemanticContent: Handling Operation identity, assigned after reservation grant and before execution.
Exact Step-specialized target occurrence reference(s), when the operation is occurrence-targeted.
Publication/reservation provenance required to prove acceptance and custody.
operationEntry.ownership: The Unit prepares the entry; the Step-specific Publisher accepts and retains it atomically; the Step-specific Error Handling Composition aggregates accepted entries.

errorHandlerResult.meaning: The Step-specific aggregate of accepted operation entries published by the selected Error Handling Unit invocation(s).

typeParameters.name: THandlingOperationEntry
typeParameters.meaning: The Step-specialized entry type used to represent one operation execution. It may be ErrorHandlingOperationEntry[THandlingOperationResult] or a Step-defined tagged union/variant when multiple Units have different operation result types.

typeParameters.name: TErrorHandlingContext
typeParameters.meaning: The Step-specific context associated with the aggregate when required; use the concrete Step context type or None when no aggregate context is required.

rules: It aggregates accepted entries only; an unaccepted or indeterminate entry is not silently included as accepted.
It preserves each entry's Unit, Association, target, invocation, attempt, operation, and result provenance.
It is distinct from ErrorResult and does not imply that any source occurrence has been resolved.
It is the TErrorHandlerResult contribution carried through StepExecutionResult.

publisherAndReservation.operationEntryPublisher: OperationEntryPublisher[THandlingOperationResult] is an invocation-scoped capability supplied by Step-specific Error Handling Composition.
publisherAndReservation.publicationReservation: PublicationReservation[THandlingOperationResult] is a Publisher-issued capability that authorizes one complete entry for one handling operation attempt and secures the concrete capacity/resources required for final transfer.
publisherAndReservation.authority: The specialized Publisher contract owns the atomic acceptance point and accepted-entry retention. The Unit does not infer acceptance from a publish call or Prefect Task State.
publisherAndReservation.detailAllocation: The exact reserve/publish/status/release state machine, no-fail transfer, recovery, identity generation, and retention requirements are specified in 11,00_Publication.json.

association.scope: The concrete Step chooses the exact target scope and Association. An Error Handling Unit invocation is bound to the exact Association selected for it; it must not infer or substitute another Association.
association.identity: Unit identity, Association identity, association target identity, and occurrence identity remain distinct.
association.flexibility: A Supporting Pattern may be associated with a Step, SPU, or another scope only where its specialized contract permits. The current Step Error Handling specialization governs only the scopes it explicitly defines.
association.termination: Ending an Association prevents new invocations under that Association but does not automatically release the Unit or revoke accepted entries.

lifecycle.unitResponsibility: The Unit performs its own preparation, readiness reporting, operation setup/shutdown, and resource release.
separation: Unit instance lifetime is distinct from Association lifetime.
Unit instance lifetime is distinct from invocation and operation lifetimes.
Publisher capability lifetime is invocation-scoped and distinct from Unit lifetime.
Accepted entries and ErrorHandlerResult may outlive the Unit instance and its Associations.
lifecycle.quiescence: Before release, Step Composition closes admission, reconciles active operations and reservations, and ensures every produced result has a known custodian or explicit unresolved Recovery Owner.
lifecycle.noManager: No generic lifecycle manager, pool, factory, or state machine is introduced.

genericPackageMustNotDefine: SPUError or StageError concrete occurrence families.
A universal error taxonomy or global registry.
errorModelIsolation.consumerSpecialization: A concrete Step supplies its own Error Model, target occurrence reference types, registries if required, and ErrorResult contract. The Error Handling Unit consumes bounded typed references supplied by that Step.
errorModelIsolation.generatorBoundary: The current Generator Common Error Model remains consumer-specific. Its pipeline-owned registry matrix and concrete error types are not dependencies of core.supporting_patterns.error_handling.
errorModelIsolation.diagnostics: A specialized operation/Publisher violation may include Diagnostic[TDetails] from optional core.diagnostics, but Error Handling does not require that package and does not interpret diagnostic details.

flowAndResultRules.noFlowOwnership: The Error Handling Unit does not control Step, Stage, or Pipeline flow.
flowAndResultRules.noResolutionClaim: A produced HandlingOperationResult or accepted ErrorHandlerResult entry does not prove that the target occurrence is resolved.
flowAndResultRules.noAutomaticConversion: A thrown exception is not automatically converted into ErrorResult, HandlingOperationResult, or ErrorHandlerResult.
flowAndResultRules.optionalContribution: The concrete ErrorHandlerResult may populate OptionalResultContributions.error_handler_result. It is never merged into error_result.
flowAndResultRules.observationSeparation: Observation Records are not Error Handling operation entries and are not included in ErrorHandlerResult unless a specialized contract explicitly defines an operation-specific observation payload.

prefectIntegrationBoundary.nativeRealization: A bounded Error Handling Unit invocation or explicitly bounded handling operation may be wrapped as a Prefect Task inside the owning Step Subworkflow.
bindingResponsibilities: Pass the exact Step-defined TErrorHandlingUnitInput and invocation-scoped Publisher capability.
Preserve Unit, Association, target, invocation, attempt, operation, and reservation identities separately from Prefect native IDs.
Return/retain the exact operation result/entry and publication acceptance evidence through the specialized Publisher protocol.
Keep Prefect Task State separate from operation result, reservation state, publication acceptance, and custody.
Do not assume one Unit invocation equals one handling operation.
Do not assume Task completion proves the complete entry was accepted or the error was resolved.
notQualified: Production Error Handling Unit binding to Prefect.
No-fail result transfer under the selected concrete Step payload types.
Ambiguous acceptance escrow and Recovery Owner implementation.
Failure, cancellation, timeout, retry, worker-loss, recovery, and safe release.

allowed: core.supporting_patterns.error_handling may depend on core.identities value contracts.
A specialized Error Handling contract may optionally depend on core.diagnostics.
The selected Step may depend on the Error Handling contract surface only when it selects the capability.
integrations.prefect may depend inward on the generic Error Handling contracts and selected specialized Step contracts.
forbidden: core.supporting_patterns.error_handling must not depend on Generator Common Error Model.
core.supporting_patterns.error_handling must not depend on Step Composition implementation.
core.supporting_patterns.error_handling must not depend on Prefect.
The generic package must not import concrete Step Error Model occurrence types.
No mandatory dependency on Validation or Observation packages.
No generic registry, manager, scheduler, global Publisher, or central mediator.

mustExpose: The generic Error Handling Unit contract.
The identity and Association value contracts needed to construct valid specialized invocations.
publicApiRequirements.optInRule: The Error Handling Public API is optional. Importing Core or using Stage/Step/SPU without Error Handling must not need this package.
mustNotExpose: A universal Error Model or concrete Generator Error types.
A global Publisher implementation or manager.
A universal handling policy or resolution Boolean.
Prefect native objects as generic Error Handling types.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: Retain MOD-CORE-SUPPORT-EH as optional_reusable; specify its generic identity/result/publication dependencies and forbid dependencies on Generator Error Model, Step Composition implementation, Prefect, and other optional patterns.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: Makes the optional package's dependency closure explicit.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.approval: Requires architecture acceptance and cross-artifact reconciliation.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: Allocate generic Error Handling contracts and publication protocol under core.supporting_patterns.error_handling without adding core.error_model or a universal supporting_units package.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: The optional capability owns its behavior and publication contracts while the consumer owns the concrete Error Model.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.approval: Requires architecture acceptance and cross-artifact reconciliation.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: No semantic change proposed; preserve its TErrorHandlingUnitInput and THandlingOperationResult specializations.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: The existing contract already expresses the generic operation boundary and publication semantics.

requiredGoverningContractChanges.change: No semantic change proposed; preserve ErrorHandlerResult[THandlingOperationEntry, TErrorHandlingContext] and its accepted-entry aggregate semantics.
requiredGoverningContractChanges.reason: The existing result contract already owns the two-parameter aggregate contract and its distinction from ErrorResult.

conformanceRequirements.requirement: Error Handling remains an optional independent Supporting Pattern.
The generic package defines no universal Error Model, Error Occurrence, Error Registry, or ErrorResult schema.
ErrorHandlingUnit uses Step/consumer-specialized input and per-operation result types.
One Unit invocation may contain zero, one, or multiple operation attempts and results.
Every actual operation result is tied to its exact attempt, operation, target, Association, and Unit invocation provenance.
The Unit does not own or mutate source Error Occurrences or ErrorResult.
ErrorHandlerResult[THandlingOperationEntry, TErrorHandlingContext] aggregates accepted operation entries and remains distinct from ErrorResult.
Publisher/Reservation acceptance and recovery custody follow the specialized protocol and are not inferred from Prefect State.
Step Composition owns Association, invocation authorization, lifecycle, and Step-specific aggregate integration.
The generic Error Handling package imports no Generator Error Model, Prefect, or Step Composition implementation.
Diagnostics remain optional descriptive evidence and do not replace Error, Failure, Exception, or Outcome semantics.
No universal Error Handling Manager, plugin registry, scheduler, global Publisher, or resolution policy is introduced.

supports: ErrorHandlingUnit is generic over Step-specific input and per-operation result.
One invocation may execute multiple operation attempts.
Reservation precedes operation execution; publication acceptance is the custody handoff point.
The Unit does not own source occurrences, ErrorResult, StepExecutionResult, or Step flow.
ErrorHandlerResult uses THandlingOperationEntry and TErrorHandlingContext generic parameters.
ErrorHandlerResult aggregates accepted operation entries and remains distinct from ErrorResult.
Error Handling Unit is a Step-owned optional Supporting Unit.
Behavior, Association, and Lifecycle contracts are distinct and specialized.
Unit identity is distinct from Association, invocation, operation, and result lifetimes.
Association identity and target identity are distinct from Unit identity.
One invocation is bound to the exact Association selected by Step Composition.
Step Composition owns lifecycle decisions and coordinates admission, quiescence, reuse, and release.
Accepted results and ErrorHandlerResult may outlive the Unit instance and its Associations.
The concrete Step must define no-fail result transfer, Recovery Owner, identity generation, status retention, and end-to-end publication traces.
Diagnostic is descriptive only and is not a universal Error, Failure, Exception, or Outcome.
Diagnostic may be used optionally by specialized Error Handling contracts.

acceptanceCriteria: Error Handling is a reusable optional capability, not a universal Error Model.
All source Error Model semantics remain with the concrete Step/consumer.
The Unit input, operation results, entries, and aggregate are explicitly typed and match the existing contract generic parameters.
Operation attempt/execution identities and Association/target provenance remain distinct.
Publisher/Reservation acceptance and recovery custody remain authoritative and separate from Prefect operational State.
ErrorHandlerResult remains distinct from ErrorResult and does not assert resolution.
Association and lifecycle remain Step Composition-owned.
No generic runtime manager, registry, scheduler, or global Publisher is introduced.
The design is consistent with the current specialized Error Handling contracts and Wave 2 optional result contribution model.
No specialized source contract is modified by this artifact.

changeControl.authority: Wave 4 detailed design proposal. It becomes an implementation constraint only after architecture review and explicit acceptance.
changeControl.sourceContractPolicy: This artifact preserves the existing ErrorHandlingUnit, ErrorHandlerResult, Association, and Lifecycle specialized contracts; it does not edit them.
changeControl.implementationGate: Do not implement or promote generic Error Handling package dependencies until Wave 4 and the concrete publication design are reviewed and accepted.
changeControl.nextStep: Review 11,00_Publication.json. It must specify the generic reservation/publication protocol boundary and the required per-Step specialization proof without choosing one universal storage or concurrency implementation.
